comment: The recorded exchanges between the browser extension and the agent. Read by internal/proxy/contract_test.go, which replays them against a real agent, and by extension/test/contract.test.ts, which drives the extension's client against them. Regenerate the responses with `make contract-update`; the requests and the `why` lines are written by hand.

exchanges.name: mask two fields of one send
exchanges.why: One pass over both texts, so the address repeated across them keeps one identity — masked field by field it would leave as two different people. The credential is tokenized alongside it, and the count includes the repeat, because a value masked twice is two values that did not leave the machine.

exchanges.name: expand a whole replacement in one chunk
exchanges.why: The ordinary case: a chunk carrying a complete token, nothing held back. A client that got this wrong would show the person their own bookkeeping.

exchanges.name: hold back what could be the start of a replacement
exchanges.why: The chunk ends mid-token. Emitting those characters would put half a token on screen and make the other half unexpandable, so they come back as a tail for the caller to carry.

exchanges.name: complete a replacement split across two chunks
exchanges.why: The tail from the call before, prepended to this chunk. This is the whole reason the protocol carries one, and a client that dropped it would restore nothing at all in a streamed answer.

exchanges.name: a replacement at the very end of the stream
exchanges.why: Half a token arriving as the last thing the model wrote. Without the flush below it is simply never shown: the person reads a sentence with its last word missing.

exchanges.name: the flush that ends the stream
exchanges.why: final:true expands the remaining tail and holds nothing back. It is the protocol's explicit end, and the one call a client is most likely to forget because everything looks right without it until a value lands last.

exchanges.name: a token nothing expands is left visible
exchanges.why: What the agent's own response path does for an answer still in flight when the mode changed and the mapping was purged. Inventing a value would put data in front of somebody that nothing supports; hiding it would hide that something went wrong.
